## Notes from the launch planning meeting

We are a team of six planning the launch of a new mobile app for booking shared desks. The app is ready for a first release. The launch is planned for the start of June.

## Why we are launching now

Our pilot ran for eight weeks with three offices. People booked a desk in under a minute. Most pilot users kept using the app after the pilot ended. The offices asked us to open it to their whole staff.

## What the first release does

- Book a desk for a day or for half a day.
- See which desks are free on a floor plan.
- Invite a colleague to sit next to you.
- Cancel a booking with one tap.

Payments and meeting rooms are not in the first release. We will look at them after the launch.

## The plan

The launch has four stages.

1. **Finish testing** in April. We test the app with five teams in each pilot office.
2. **Train the office managers** in early May. Each office has one manager who answers questions.
3. **Open the app** to the three pilot offices at the start of June.
4. **Review the launch** at the end of June, and decide which offices come next.

## Who does what

The product lead owns the launch date and the scope. The design lead owns the floor plans and the help pages. Two developers fix the bugs found in testing. The support lead trains the office managers. The data lead reports how many desks are booked each week.

## Risks

The floor plans may be out of date in one office. We will walk each floor before the launch and correct the plans.

Some people may not want to install another app. The app also works in the browser, so nobody has to install it.

Testing may find more bugs than the two developers can fix in April. If it does, we move the launch by two weeks rather than cut the testing.

## What we ask of the offices

Each office names one manager by the end of April. Each office sends us its latest floor plans. Each office tells its staff about the launch one week before it opens.

## How we will know it worked

We want half of the staff in each office to book a desk in the first month. We want fewer than ten support questions a week after the second week. We will share the numbers at the review at the end of June.
